title: Branching Fundamentals
introduction: In professional development, nobody writes code directly on `main`. Today you learn **branching** — Git's superpower that lets you create isolated parallel timelines to build features or fix bugs without risking the stability of your working application.
why_it_matters: Branches allow 10 or 1,000 developers to work on the exact same codebase at the same time without stepping on each other's toes. Because Git branches are lightweight 41-byte pointer files, creating or switching branches is nearly instantaneous.
practical_activity_preview: Create a feature branch, make commits in isolation, and switch between branches.
